identity.name: Rafael S. de Souza
identity.biography: I am an astrophysicist working across astronomy, statistics, mathematics and computation. My work spans galaxy structure, spatially resolved spectroscopy, statistical inference and scientific representations. I founded the Cosmostatistics Initiative (COIN), have held international leadership roles in astrostatistics, and co-authored the award-winning Bayesian Models for Astrophysical Data.

art.alt: Astronomical artwork with nebular contours in teal and ochre

introduction.statement: I have always been drawn to the places where one way of seeing the world becomes another.
introduction.body: I study what astronomical observations can distinguish when information is incomplete, selectively sampled, compressed, or structured across wavelength and position. Much of my work begins with a simple question: what structure in the data are our usual methods failing to see?

research_objects.title: A break in the Milky Way’s Sagittarius Arm

figure.alt: Diagram of the Milky Way showing a high-pitch-angle structure protruding from the Sagittarius Arm

research_objects.body: Twenty-five star-forming regions reveal a narrow structure about one kiloparsec long, oriented at roughly 56° to the Galactic azimuth, compared with about 12° for the surrounding Sagittarius Arm.

research_objects.title: Coherent regions in resolved galaxies

figure.alt: Five MaNGA galaxies and their spectral segmentation maps

research_objects.body: CAPIVARA groups spaxels by spectral similarity and maps them back onto the galaxy. In five MaNGA systems, the recovered regions were coherent in continuum and emission-line properties without imposing a bulge–disc decomposition.

research_objects.title: Spectra as ordered geometric objects

figure.alt: Normalised line profiles and their widths and shape coordinates in the spectropath toy case

research_objects.body: Spectral lines with similar widths can differ in absorption, asymmetry and the ordering of their components. spectropath describes these differences through a path in velocity–flux space.
